questions.q: Why does search-as-you-type call for an imperative Apex call rather than @wire, per this lesson's reasoning?
options: Because Apex search methods can never be marked cacheable=true
Because @wire does not support any Apex method with string parameters

Because the search is triggered by a specific user action (typing) that changes constantly, and the developer wants direct control over exactly when the call fires rather than a live subscription re-provisioning on every keystroke
Because imperative calls are required whenever NavigationMixin is used
questions.explain: This directly applies Lesson 18's reasoning: a user-triggered, frequently-changing action is exactly the case for an imperative call, giving direct control over timing rather than letting @wire's reactive re-provisioning fire on every keystroke.

questions.q: What problem does debouncing solve in the record search tool?
options: It prevents the Apex method from ever returning more than one result
It replaces the need for an imperative Apex call entirely
It automatically formats the search results into a lightning-datatable
It avoids firing a separate server round trip on every single keystroke by waiting for a short pause in typing before actually calling Apex
questions.explain: Without debouncing, a word typed quickly could trigger several wasted server calls, most immediately superseded by the next keystroke. Debouncing waits for a pause before firing, canceling any pending wait if the user keeps typing.

questions.q: Why does this lesson's design call for an 'object-agnostic' Apex search method and configuration, rather than hardcoding one object?
options: Because Apex cannot query more than one object type in a single org
Because @AuraEnabled methods are not allowed to take object API names as parameters

Because the whole point of the tool is that an admin configures which object it searches without a developer rewriting code per object -- requiring a generic method signature and an admin-configurable objectApiName property
Because object-agnostic methods run faster than object-specific ones in every case
questions.explain: The reusability goal -- an admin dropping the tool on any object's record page without a code change -- requires a generic method and a configurable objectApiName property, directly applying Lesson 23's generic-component thinking and Lesson 27's targetConfig pattern.

questions.q: How does this lesson suggest testing the debounce logic without waiting in real time during the test run?
options: By using fake timers (e.g. jest.useFakeTimers()) to advance simulated time and confirm the Apex call only fires once after rapid simulated typing
By manually running the test suite multiple times over several minutes
Debounce logic cannot be unit tested at all and requires manual QA only
By disabling the debounce entirely inside the test environment
questions.explain: Jest's fake timers let a test advance simulated time instantly, confirming the debounced behavior (one call after a pause, not one per keystroke) without the test actually waiting in real time.

questions.q: Which accessibility requirement does this lesson call out specifically for the search input and its results?
options: The search input needs no label at all, since its purpose is visually obvious
Only screen magnification support is required, not keyboard support
Accessibility only matters for the NavigationMixin portion of the component
The search input needs a real label (or alternative-text if icon-only), and results must be reachable and selectable by keyboard, not mouse-only
questions.explain: Per Lesson 30's accessibility principles applied here, the search input needs a proper label (or alternative-text), and the results list must be usable via keyboard, not only by mouse click.
